BLOOM 9–14
Transcend · Portfolio Story

WE NAMED IT
BLOOM.

High school is when young people open. The stretch from 9th grade through the early years after, college, career, the first real taste of adult life, is one connected season of growth. Bloom 9–14 partners with school communities to redesign that season so every young person reaches it as a thriving young adult.

Our bet

HIGH SCHOOL REDESIGN NEEDS PROTECTED R&D SPACE, NETWORKED WITH OTHERS DOING THE SAME WORK.

Schools have to keep the current model running while inventing a new one. That is hard to do alone. So we build small protected spaces inside real schools where teams can rethink time, adult roles, assessment, and technology, then connect those schools so they learn faster together than any one could alone. That bet now has a name. The Design Commons.

Logic Model v3 · The four-layer evidence framework

HOW WE KNOW IT'S WORKING

Different kinds of work produce different kinds of proof. A district pilot, a codified model, and a cross-school sprint do not generate the same evidence. So we look at growth in four layers, from the conditions we build to the lives young people lead.

The design journey

EVERY PLANT FOLLOWS THE SAME SEASONS

LEARN

Empathy interviews, inspiration visits, current-state research. Looking outward before deciding anything.

ENVISION

Name the future-state student experience the community wants. Align on direction.

BUILD

Design specific pilots. Scope, sequence, and the conditions a real test needs.

TRY

Put it in front of students. Gather data. Iterate. Then decide what scales.

Learning agenda · FY26

WHAT WE'RE LEARNING

A portfolio is only as honest as the questions it's willing to sit with. These are ours. Each one carries a hypothesis we hold loosely, the evidence that would change our mind, and how confident we actually are right now. Most confidence is low. That's not a gap in the work. It's the work.

Confidence in our current hypothesis Low Low–Medium Medium

No question here is rated higher than Medium. We don't have Layer 3 outcome evidence for most of this work yet, and we'd rather say so than dress up early signals as proof.
